subject: Re: Order Form — Tiered Volume Escrow & Price-lock Carveout (redlines)
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@magnetohealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Magneto Health Legal <legal@magnetohealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Revised redline — escrow mechanics and release schedule

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redline of the Order Form (magneto_redline_orderform_v1.pdf) and a short Excel schedule showing the proposed escrow math (Escrow_Terms_Schedule.xlsx). High level ask: we want a pricing-stability escrow to smooth short‑term volatility while we stand up volume commitments. Key points from our side:

- Hold 5% of monthly invoice amounts in an escrow (reserve) administered by the parties.
- Monthly releases: 50% of the previous month’s reserve released monthly, remainder reconciled on quarterly true‑up.
- Escrow to be held only during the first 12 months of the term; automatic release on month 13 unless a true‑up finds underpayment.
- If Redwood asserts a price increase, Magneto can trigger an audit (once per year) with 30 days’ notice.
- We want an explicit floor so our effective unit price cannot exceed the listed maximum for the first 18 months.

Please review and confirm whether this approach is acceptable or whether you need the escrow to be structured as a credit rather than a segregated hold. We’re happy to jump on a call with legal if helpful.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Procurement, Magneto Health
emily.chen@magnetohealth.com
+1 415-555-0124

Attachment: magneto_redline_orderform_v1.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: Escrow_Terms_Schedule.xlsx (Excel)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@magnetohealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised redline — escrow mechanics and release schedule

Emily — thanks for sending this over and for the clear schedule. I’ve looped Aditya (AE) so he can keep the commercial calendar aligned. A few quick clarifying Qs before we take this to legal:

1) Is the 5% reserve intended as a cash escrow held in a third‑party account or as a billing credit that stays on Magneto’s ledger?
2) You mentioned an explicit floor — can you confirm whether that’s a fixed per‑token price floor or a monthly spend floor?

Short read from my side: we’re broadly open to a temporary reserve to smooth onboarding risk, but holding 5% of gross monthly invoices for 12 months is higher than we typically accept. I’ll send an internal redline proposing a compromise (6‑month reserve at 3–4%) and will cc legal for terms language.

I’ve attached a quick internal stub we’ll use as a starting point. Let me know if Magneto has any non‑negotiable constraints.

Best,
Lauren
Business Lead, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Attachment: internal_stub_escrow_notes.txt (text)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised redline — escrow mechanics and release schedule

Thanks for the tag, Lauren — I reviewed Magneto’s PDF and the Excel schedule. High‑level legal flags and proposed edits (summary):

- Characterization of funds: Magneto’s redline frames the hold as an escrow administered by the parties. We have operational concerns about segregated third‑party escrow (bank relationships, interest treatment). Recommend rewording to "Reserve Account" that is a billing hold applied to the contract and subject to reconciliation.

- Cap on exposure: Do not accept open‑ended escrow amounts. Limit reserve to the greater of 3% of recurring monthly invoice or $50k, with a rolling cap not to exceed 3% of trailing 12‑month ARR.

- Trigger and clawback: Allow clawback only for manifest billing errors or undisputed underpayments >5% of the reserved amount. No clawback for normal usage variance.

- Release schedule/true‑up: Propose quarterly true‑up (not monthly) with any remaining reserve released within 30 days of reconciliation. This reduces operational churn.

- Termination: If Magneto terminates for convenience prior to month 12, Redwood may apply final true‑up and retain amounts necessary to cure unpaid usage; remaining reserve returned within 45 days.

- Audit rights: Accept one audit per 12 months limited to billing records; require 30 days’ notice and confidentiality protections.

I attached a Word with inline redlines (orderform_redline_rishi.docx). If you want to accept the reserve framing we can draft exhibit language that limits both the dollar exposure and the operational burden.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Attachment: orderform_redline_rishi.docx (Word)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@magnetohealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Magneto Health Legal <legal@magnetohealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised redline — escrow mechanics and release schedule

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Rishi. A couple responses from procurement/legal here:  

- We can accept the "Reserve Account" language provided the operational release cadence remains monthly (Magneto relies on monthly reconciliations for internal forecast). Quarterly true‑ups add material cash timing risk for us.
- Magneto cannot accept a hard cap expressed as % of ARR — that will tie our hands. We are willing to accept a dollar cap (e.g., $150k) tied to the initial 12‑month forecast, with a right to re‑open if actuals materially exceed forecast ( >25% variance).
- Clawback: we can accept a manifest error threshold but request that the threshold be 3% (not 5%) of the reserved amount.

We attached a counter spreadsheet with suggested numbers (counter_proposals.xlsx). Also, we’re open to a joint escrow admin (neutral third party) if Redwood insists on a segregated account.

If we can land on the numbers above, Procurement can push the order form through to signature next week.

—Emily

Attachment: counter_proposals.xlsx (Excel)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@magnetohealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Revised redline — escrow mechanics and release schedule

Emily — thanks, this is helpful and makes the path to signature clearer. Proposed commercial compromise from Redwood to present to Magneto legal: 

- Reserve Account (billing hold) vs. segregated escrow: accept "Reserve Account" language; no third‑party bank escrow.
- Exposure cap: $125,000 initial cap tied to first 12‑month forecast, with a mutual re‑forecast right on >25% variance.
- Reserve percentage: 4% of monthly invoices or the $125k cap, whichever is lower.
- Release cadence: monthly releases (as requested) with a quarterly reconciliation true‑up; remaining balance returned within 30 days of true‑up.
- Clawback threshold: 4% of reserved amount for manifest errors.
- Audit: one audit per 12 months with 30 days’ notice; Redwood to redact any proprietary model performance metrics not relevant to billing.
- Price‑lock carveout: to address unexpected infrastructure cost jumps, Redwood proposes a temporary surcharge trigger: if Redwood’s model execution costs (GPU & infra) increase by >20% for three consecutive months due to market events, parties will meet to negotiate an interim surcharge not to exceed 2% of each month’s invoice; surcharge sunsets after 90 days or on next pricing review.

If Magneto accepts these points we’ll prepare final redline exhibits and a DocuSign packet for procurement. I’ve opened a DocuSign placeholder here: https://www.docusign.com/link/ABCDEF123456 (final link will be sent once language is agreed).

Can you confirm today so Aditya can get procurement aligned?

Thanks,
Lauren
Business Lead, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Lauren — this looks workable. Procurement is prepared to proceed on the commercial terms you outlined with two small asks: 

1) Increase the initial cap to $135,000 (to account for our onboarding consumption variance).
2) Clarify SLA credit interaction: any surcharge invoked under the Price‑lock carveout should be net of SLA credits for downtime caused by Redwood.

If Redwood can accept those tweaks we’ll push the redline to our procurement signature queue and provide a final PO. Please have legal update the exhibit and resend the DocuSign link; once we have the final exhibits we expect approval within 48 hours.

We’ll also need a short operational runbook explaining reconciliation cadence and the person at Redwood who will receive audit requests. Can you include that in the DocuSign packet?

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

—Emily
